gen-dafont-alien-encounters-gf-montserra: Round, chalky lowercase with a wide-open c makes Montserrat Alternates easy going on the eye. Alien Encounters is the otherworldly one, earning its place when the words are big and few, spaced out like signal beacons.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-cascadia-mono: Azonix has capitals barely taller than its lowercase, so words take a beat to knit together. Cascadia Mono answers with compact letters standing like pins in a wide board, with rounded curves as thick as its stems.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-julius-sans-one: Julius Sans One spreads its letters across big stretches of blank space, with curves left open at the ends. And Azonix gives that lightness a commanding top line, wide-mouthed and crisp even when shrunk.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-lexend-exa: Azonix has wide-mouthed letters that stay crisp when shrunk, though its capitals sit only slightly above the lowercase and words need a moment to knit. Lexend Exa does the quieter job: wide curves, a big x-height, stubby ascenders.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-lexend-giga: Flat, wide, and a little military. Azonix gives the heading command, while Lexend Giga follows with generous tracking that opens each word and ascenders that barely clear the x-height, all in single-weight linework.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-lexend-mega: Wide stance, bold attitude. Azonix is the heading font for commanding, crisp lines; Lexend Mega is the one for text, drawn as if with one nib, its lowercase nearly as tall as the capitals.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-lexend-peta: Azonix brings authority with wide-mouthed letters and capitals only slightly taller than its lowercase, so words take a moment to knit. But Lexend Peta loosens things up, its curves never thinning and its big x-height squeezing the ascenders.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-lexend-tera: Hard-edged and wide, Azonix commands the top, its capitals only slightly above the lowercase, so words need a moment to knit back together. Lexend Tera then reads like plotter-pen lines, spaced like stepping stones.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-lexend-zetta: Tall-bodied, widely tracked small letters make Lexend Zetta read like cut ribbon, constant in width. Its strongest quality is how that openness lets Azonix stay the commanding, wide-mouthed voice up top.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-montserrat-alternat: Montserrat Alternates has a c as open as a bent paperclip. Azonix is best at commanding, crisp headings that survive shrinking, while the body font's round, chalk-board lowercase is best at friendly, steady running text.
